mechanism_narrative: A sustained quarterly increase in GDP (GDPC1) signals expanding economic activity, which lowers discount rates and boosts equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) in 60% of instances where GDPC1 rises, or the GDP growth rate does not exceed 2% quarterly.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 7.5% triggers investor concerns about labor market weakness, causing short-term negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 20d returns remain negative despite UNRATE crossing above 7.5%, or the effect persists beyond 5 days without reversal.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and GDP (GDPC1) indicates dual accommodative monetary and demand-driven growth, amplifying equity valuations and generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and GDPC1 both rising for 3 months
failure_condition: Interaction effect not statistically significant (p > 0.05) in 3-year walk-forward test, or returns are not positive in >60% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (rising FEDFUNDS), investors anticipate higher interest rates, reducing equity valuations and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20d returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during FEDFUNDS tightening periods, or the effect reverses before 20 days.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in supply (INDPRO) and decline in unemployment (UNRATE) signals robust economic expansion, boosting corporate profits and equity prices, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO↑ and UNRATE↓ in the same month
failure_condition: Interaction effect not statistically significant (p > 0.05) in 6-month walk-forward, or returns not positive in >70% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden surge in the CPIAUCSL index above 231.25 signals accelerating inflation, prompting central banks to tighten policy and reducing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20d returns remain non-negative despite CPIAUCSL crossing above 231.25, or the effect fades within 20 days.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in employment (PAYEMS) reflects strong labor market conditions, boosting consumer spending and corporate profits, which drive positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60d returns not significantly positive (p > 0.05) during periods of sustained employment growth, or the effect diminishes over time.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion characterized by low unemployment (UNRATE < 6.0%), investors anticipate prolonged growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20d returns not significantly positive (p > 0.05) during UNRATE <6% periods, or the effect reverses before 20 days.
